newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London steady, Dow seen lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London steady, Dow seen lower.

text.p: U.S. stocks in London were steady to slightly lower on Wednesday as the market digested the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave rates unchanged and mulled over the weakness of the Dow and the dollar.
"It's surprisingly quiet at the moment...I think the market has really gone into "wait and see' mode. Most had expected the Fed to make a move on rates," one dealer said.

Traders said the Fed's inaction had pulled the prospect of third-quarter earnings back into focus, with worries fuelled by a shock profit warning from telecoms group AT&T Corp and the impact of the weaker dollar.
AT&T's weakness weighed on the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which closed 20.71 points lower at 5,874.03. Traders said the Dow was likely to open slightly lower on Wednesday.
Dealers said AT&T, which dropped $5-3/4 to $51-1/2 overnight, was trading $1/4 higher in London at $51-3/4.
"The one thing that hit Wall Street was the question mark over third-quarter earnings, particularly at AT&T," Sonja Shechter, European equity strategist at Daiwa Europe Ltd, said.
Shechter said the market could enter a holding pattern amid debate about earnings. The Fed inaction also meant uncertainty about a still-expected tightening would overshadow the market.
"People will get even more jittery about economic data," Shechter said.
Among other movers in London, Texas Instruments was down $1/8 at $57-1/4. The stock gained heavily overnight and was upgraded to buy from hold by Montgomery Securities.
